captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/11_cpc, specifically its paper-faithful visual_cpc2018 path (models/visual_cpc2018.py, data/visual_cpc2018_dataset.py, train_pretrain_visual_cpc2018.py) and its unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (models/cpc_vit.py, train_step2_vit.py, configs/step2_vit.yaml). These are the lab's own implementation of van den Oord et al. (2018) visual CPC, torch/torchvision (plus timm for the ViT). So it ports self-contained (no third_party submodule). The capture directory number (11) equals this method's number in the Step 1&2 list (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding

scope: The capture ships two step-1 variants. The older local baseline (cpc_resnet: a custom residual encoder with BatchNorm and a column-wise GRU) is documented by the capture's own CPC_STEP1_PAPER_READY_BLOCK.md as a structural protocol mismatch that 'must not be submitted as a paper-ready Step 1 job' (its ImageNet linear-eval reaches only 6.4% top-1 vs the paper's ~48.7%). It is EXCLUDED. This port brings across the corrected visual_cpc2018 path: a ResNet-v2-101-style no-BN patch encoder, a PixelCNN-style masked-convolution context, and log-bilinear InfoNCE over future rows of the patch grid. The capture's unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 is also ported additively (arch: vit; models/vit_cpc.py, train_pretrain_vit_cpc.py, configs/pretrain_vit.yaml): the ViT's patch tokens as the CPC z-grid, a column-GRU context, k linear predictors under InfoNCE, probed at the ViT CLS token; the native visual_cpc2018 path is byte-for-byte unchanged. The ViT path adds timm.
encoder: For the native visual_cpc2018 path, encoder.pt is the patch encoder (encoder.*): conv1 + three pre-activation bottleneck stages (3, 4, 23 blocks, no BatchNorm) with a projection to z_dim, producing a z-vector per patch. For the Step-2 ViT path, encoder.pt is the ViT trunk (encoder.*), loaded into a plain timm VisionTransformer and probed at its CLS token, plus encoder_epoch{100,200,300}.pt per milestone. In both, the context (context.*) and the InfoNCE predictors (predictors.*) are pretext machinery and are left out.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the grid-averaged z (avg_z, z_dim-d) -- the mean of the encoder's per-patch z over the patch grid, a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Patch grids use the deterministic val pipeline (centre crop, no per-patch augmentation). Follows the lab's ARSSL probe (L2-normalise + mean-centre, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5). The capture's own eval offers avg_z / avg_context / concat modes and an SGD-milestone schedule; this port fixes avg_z with the shared ARSSL probe for a comparable number.
rewritten_during_the_port: the paper-faithful visual_cpc2018 path is the native port and the capture's unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (arch: vit) is ported additively; the deprecated local baseline (cpc_resnet) is excluded

models/vit_cpc.py is port-authored from the capture's models/cpc_vit.py: a timm VisionTransformer (num_classes=0, global_pool='') under self.encoder, a column-wise GRU context and pred_steps linear predictors. The ViT trunk lives under encoder. so encoder.pt keeps encoder.* -- the same prefix as the native patch encoder -- and get_encoder() returns the CLS feature. The ViT dims are threaded into VisionTransformer (the capture built the fixed vit_base_patch16_224) so a tiny hermetic CPU smoke can run; z_dim is required to equal embed_dim (the z-grid IS the ViT's patch tokens). timm is imported lazily on arch: vit.

train_pretrain_vit_cpc.py is a single-process port of the capture's train_step2_vit.py: the lr is used directly (the capture baked lr=1.5e-4*1024/256=6e-4 into the config), AdamW with weight decay 0.05, a linear warmup then cosine decay to min_lr, and milestone checkpoints (checkpoint_epoch_{N}.pth at save_at_epochs). It reuses resolve_device/make_deterministic from the native trainer; DDP and TensorBoard are dropped. The train transform is the capture's (RandomResizedCrop + flip + colour jitter + grayscale + ImageNet normalise).

the adapter gained an arch: vit branch (disjoint key sets from the native path), a ViT load_encoder branch, milestone encoder_epoch{N}.pt extraction, and an arch: vit linear_eval; configs/pretrain_vit.yaml and configs/linear_eval_vit.yaml are added. evaluate_linear_cpc2018.py is arch-aware: the ViT path builds a plain ImageFolder val loader (resize + centre crop + ImageNet normalise) and probes the CLS token, not the native patch grid.
requirements.txt gained a timm floor (timm>=0.9.0); the CPU and cu130 locks close over torch/torchvision/numpy/PyYAML/timm at the fleet versions (the same closure as 13_mocov1).
the dataset's hard-coded 7x7 grid check is relaxed to any grid of at least 2x2, so a small hermetic CPU smoke can run; the paper's 7x7 geometry is still what the shipped config asks for
the InfoNCE cross-rank all-gather (DistributedDataParallel) path is kept behind a flag but defaults off, so negatives come from within the batch in the single-process port
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext InfoNCE loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, AMP and TensorBoard so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; step-1 reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
